# Cross-platform lab fixture

`Get-XplatEvidence` in `tests/TestHelpers.ps1` builds this lab in memory. It is the input for the
security graph and blast-radius tests (`tests/Graph.Tests.ps1`). No file in this folder is read at
run time; the lab is assembled from the existing fixtures so each platform stays defined in one
place.

| Part | Source | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| vCenter, ESXi hosts, vSphere VMs | `tests/fixtures/demo-evidence.json` (generated by `build/New-DemoEvidence.ps1`) | `ep-vc01` |
| NSX Manager, segments, DFW policy | same demo evidence | `ep-nsx01` |
| Hyper-V host `hv01`, cluster `hvclu01`, VMs | `tests/fixtures/hyperv-collector.json` (imported) | `ep-hv01` |
| KVM host `kvm01`, libvirt VMs and networks | `tests/fixtures/kvm-collector.txt` (imported) | `ep-kvm01` |

## The cross-platform hop

The fixture moves the vCenter appliance onto Hyper-V:

- The vCenter endpoint `ep-vc01` records `resolvedAddresses = ["10.0.0.99"]`. The demo lab does not
  use this address: `dc01` is 10.0.0.10 and the vSphere VM `vcsa01` is 10.0.0.20.
- The first Hyper-V VM is renamed `vcsa-hv01`, so it does not collide with the vSphere VM `vcsa01`.
  Its adapter reports 10.0.0.99.

The graph links `vcsa-hv01` to vCenter with an `embodies` edge of confidence `correlated`. The name
plays no part in this: only the recorded IP matches. The path that follows is Hyper-V admin, then
the Hyper-V host, then the VM, then vCenter, then every ESXi host.

## Identity

The scope declares `identityDomains = [{ netbios = "EXAMPLE"; dns = "example.local" }]`. Domain
principals such as `EXAMPLE\Domain Admins` (Hyper-V Administrators) and `EXAMPLE\vi-admins` (vCenter
Admin) get `ad:` keys and join across platforms. Local accounts, such as `HV01\Administrator`,
`VSPHERE.LOCAL\Administrator` and the KVM `libvirt` members `ops` and `jdoe`, are namespaced per
endpoint and never join.

## Preparation

The helper runs the same steps as the analysis pipeline before rule evaluation: NSX discovery,
correlation (which resolves the NSX compute-manager registration into a `manages` relationship to
`ep-vc01:root`) and scope annotations (criticality and zones).

## Evidence gaps

The Hyper-V and KVM endpoints are imported, not connected, so they have no recorded resolved
address. The graph therefore lists them in `needsEvidence` as `embodies` candidates with the
missing fact `endpoint.resolvedAddresses`. It creates no edge for them.

## 2.0 package

`tests/fixtures/evidence-2.0.json` is a frozen copy of the demo evidence as the 2.2.0 generator
wrote it (`schemaVersion` "2.0"). Use it for tests that need a 2.0 package, such as replay and
baseline compatibility. Never regenerate it.
